In mathematics, specifically in [[order theory]] and [[functional analysis]], a '''locally convex vector lattice (LCVL)''' is a [[topological vector lattice]] that is also a [[locally convex]] space.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 
LCVLs are important in the theory of [[topological vector lattice]]s.

== Lattice semi-norms ==

The [[Minkowski functional]] of a convex, [[absorbing set|absorbing]], and [[solid set|solid]] set is a called a '''lattice semi-norm'''. 
Equivalently, it is a [[semi-norm]] <math>p</math> such that <math>|y| \leq |x|</math> implies <math>p(y) \leq p(x).</math> 
The topology of a locally convex vector lattice is generated by the family of all continuous lattice semi-norms.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 

== Properties ==

Every locally convex vector lattice possesses a neighborhood base at the origin consisting of [[convex set|convex]] [[balanced set|balanced]] [[solid set|solid]] [[absorbing set|absorbing]] sets.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 

The strong dual of a locally convex vector lattice <math>X</math> is an [[order complete]] locally convex vector lattice (under its canonical order) and it is a [[solid set|solid]] subspace of the [[Order dual (functional analysis)|order dual]] of <math>X</math>; 
moreover, if <math>X</math> is a [[barreled space]] then the continuous dual space of <math>X</math> is a band in the order dual of <math>X</math> and the strong dual of <math>X</math> is a complete locally convex TVS.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 

If a locally convex vector lattice is [[barreled space|barreled]] then its strong dual space is complete (this is not necessarily true if the space is merely a locally convex barreled space but not a locally convex vector lattice).{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 

If a locally convex vector lattice <math>X</math> is [[semi-reflexive]] then it is order complete and <math>X_b</math> (that is, <math>\left( X, b\left(X, X^{\prime}\right) \right)</math>) is a complete TVS; 
moreover, if in addition every positive linear functional on <math>X</math> is continuous then <math>X</math> is of <math>X</math> is of [[Minimal vector lattice|minimal type]], the [[Order topology (functional analysis)|order topology]] <math>\tau_{\operatorname{O}}</math> on <math>X</math> is equal to the [[Mackey topology]] <math>\tau\left(X, X^{\prime}\right),</math> and <math>\left(X, \tau_{\operatorname{O}}\right)</math> is [[Reflexive space|reflexive]].{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 
Every [[reflexive space|reflexive]] locally convex vector lattice is [[order complete]] and a complete locally convex TVS whose strong dual is a [[barreled space|barreled]] reflexive locally convex TVS that can be identified under the canonical evaluation map with the strong bidual (that is, the strong dual of the strong dual).{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 

If a locally convex vector lattice <math>X</math> is an [[infrabarreled]] TVS then it can be identified under the evaluation map with a topological vector sublattice of its strong bidual, which is an order complete locally convex vector lattice under its canonical order.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}}

If <math>X</math> is a [[Separable space|separable]] [[Metrizable topological vector space|metrizable]] [[Locally convex  topological vector space|locally convex]] [[ordered topological vector space]] whose positive cone <math>C</math> is a complete subset of <math>X,</math> then the set of [[quasi-interior point]]s of <math>C</math> is dense in <math>C.</math>{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}} 

{{math theorem|name=Theorem{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
Suppose that <math>X</math> is an [[order complete]] locally convex vector lattice with topology <math>\tau</math> and endow the bidual <math>X^{\prime\prime}</math> of <math>X</math> with its natural topology (that is, the topology of uniform convergence on equicontinuous subsets of <math>X^{\prime}</math>) and canonical order (under which it becomes an order complete locally convex vector lattice). The following are equivalent: 
<ol>
<li>The evaluation map <math>X \to X^{\prime\prime}</math> induces an isomorphism of <math>X</math> with an order complete sublattice of <math>X^{\prime\prime}.</math></li>
<li>For every majorized and directed subset <math>S</math> of <math>X,</math> the section filter of <math>S</math> converges in <math>(X, \tau)</math> (in which case it necessarily converges to <math>\sup S</math>).</li>
<li>Every [[order convergent]] filter in <math>X</math> converges in <math>(X, \tau)</math> (in which case it necessarily converges to its order limit).</li>
</ol>
}}

{{math theorem|name=Corollary{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=234–242}}|note=|style=|math_statement=
Let <math>X</math> be an [[order complete]] vector lattice with a [[regular order (mathematics)|regular order]]. The following are equivalent:
<ol>
<li><math>X</math> is of [[Minimal vector lattice|minimal type]].</li>
<li>For every [[majorized]] and direct subset <math>S</math> of <math>X,</math> the section filter of <math>S</math> converges in <math>X</math> when <math>X</math> is endowed with the [[Order topology (functional analysis)|order topology]].</li>
<li>Every [[order convergent]] filter in <math>X</math> converges in <math>X</math> when <math>X</math> is endowed with the [[Order topology (functional analysis)|order topology]].</li>
</ol>
Moreover, if <math>X</math> is of minimal type then the order topology on <math>X</math> is the finest locally convex topology on <math>X</math> for which every order convergent filter converges. 
}}

If <math>(X, \tau)</math> is a locally convex vector lattice that is [[bornological space|bornological]] and [[sequentially complete]], then there exists a family of compact spaces <math>\left(X_{\alpha}\right)_{\alpha \in A}</math> and a family of <math>A</math>-indexed vector lattice embeddings <math>f_{\alpha} : C_{\R}\left(K_{\alpha}\right) \to X</math> such that <math>\tau</math> is the finest locally convex topology on <math>X</math> making each <math>f_{\alpha}</math> continuous.{{sfn|Schaefer|Wolff|1999|pp=242–250}} 

== Examples ==

Every [[Banach lattice]], [[normed lattice]], and [[Fréchet lattice]] is a locally convex vector lattice.
